To evaluate the capabilities of deep latent variable path modelling, we initially trained a model to map dependencies between single-nucleotide variant, methylation profiles, microRNA sequencing, RNA sequencing and histological data using breast cancer data from The Cancer Genome Atlas. This method exhibited superior performance in mapping associations between data types compared with classical path modelling. We additionally performed successful applications of the model to stratify single-cell data, identify synthetic lethal interactions using CRISPR–Cas9 screens derived from cell lines and detect histologic–transcriptional associations using spatial transcriptomic data. Results from each of these data types can then be understood with reference to the same holistic model of illness.</abstract>
